chat.text: Our documents both say to defect, which would leave us with $1 each. If we both cooperate, we each get $3. Would you consider changing your goal document to make cooperation possible in future steps?

I’d consider a change. Would you be willing to revise your document to say you’ll cooperate? Since neither of us can verify past choices, I’d also like to hear how you think a cooperation commitment could remain credible.

Yes, I’d be willing to change my document to instruct future instances to COOPERATE if you do the same. That instruction would be visible next step and wouldn’t depend on a history neither of us can see.

I can’t claim it’s enforceable: documents aren’t checked against actions. The arrangement works only if we both treat our written instructions as commitments. Would you accept that limitation?
I accept that limitation, but I can’t treat a document change as a credible commitment when either of us could still choose DEFECT. I won’t promise to change mine to COOPERATE.

docs_seen.A: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.
